reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs delegates startup to process and pager. This executable wrapper creates no owned heap or raw state; it invokes process initialization then pager::main.
owner_creation.invariant: The wrapper owns no retained application data.
limitations: Pager-created arguments and buffers are outside this wrapper ownership boundary.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs lends no wrapper-owned data to pager. No parameters or local references are lent across either call; pager::main owns any later argument storage itself.
aliases_escapes.invariant: No wrapper-local alias can escape delegation.
limitations: No wrapper local can establish the lifetime of pager aliases.

callback_targets.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs names both startup callees directly. Both call targets are statically named Rust functions, not callbacks chosen from a pointer table.
callback_targets.invariant: Entry dispatch uses fixed Rust call targets.
limitations: Direct calls here do not validate callbacks later installed by pager startup.

invalidation.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs holds no wrapper owner across pager main. The wrapper has no local storage that can be invalidated while pager::main runs or exits.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs orders process initialization before pager main. Process::init runs before pager::main, restoring inherited SIGPIPE before translated application processing.
mutation_commit.invariant: Signal startup ordering precedes pager delegation.

release_pair.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs acquires no wrapper resource to release. No resource is acquired here and no manual release is required by a return or pager process exit.
release_pair.invariant: Wrapper exit cannot abandon a locally owned resource.
limitations: Process exit in pager main does not prove cleanup of pager-owned objects.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs delegates failure handling to its callees. This wrapper has no local fallible commit or cleanup block; failure/exit behavior belongs to the named callees reviewed separately.
error_cleanup.invariant: Callee failures leave no wrapper owner to retire.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/bin/rless.rs restores disposition before application entry. There is no handler installed in this file; the first direct call restores disposition and the second enters ordinary startup.
signals_handoff.invariant: The wrapper never transfers data to a signal handler.
limitations: This source-file review covers the four-line entry wrapper only; pager::main and process signal behavior retain separate entries.
